thread:
priya: CI alert: a100-smoke on patch 0c3f8 is red — 2/3 shards failed during warmup with a GPU pagefault. filing here before I dig deeper. stack / dmesg attached below. can someone kick a rerun or advise quick checks? :eyes:

ci-bot: build: a100-smoke #4421 failed on shard 1/3 — https://ci.internal/reports/4421 — exit code 137

liam: can you paste the tail of dmesg from the failing node? also which driver was in the node image?

priya: tail of dmesg from node-a100-canary-7:
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: GPU at 0000:af:00: GPU-7b2f...
[ 1234.568012] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:af:00): 13, PID=8421, GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 1234.568115] pcieport 0000:3e:00.0: AER: Corrected error received: id=00e0
[ 1234.568220] audit: type=1327 audit(1617891234.568:456): proctitle="/usr/local/bin/python3 ../serve.py"
[ 1234.568330] [drm] GPU fault(omap) on process serve.py, reason: pagefault
```

priya: node image used: redwood/gpu-runtime:cuda12-rolling (we default to latest runtime in canary)

sasha: this looks like a pagefault / GPU hang rather than straight OOM. could be a driver/runtime mismatch or a bad PTX kernel after the PR changed a fused op. do we know if the job pulled a new model artifact with different CUDA sm target?

priya: model artifact unchanged (version v1.8.2). the only diffs in the PR are batching heuristics in the runtime. no kernel code touched AFAICT.

ryan: two quick things to try: 1) rerun the failing shard pinned to the last-known-good driver (525.xx) to see if it reproduces; 2) run the same job with --batching=off to rule out the batching hotpath. I can kick a rerun with driver pin if you want.

priya: please kick the pinned rerun (thanks). also I'll queue a non-batched run.

ryan: /rerun 4421 --shard=1 --driver=525.105.17 --note="pin-driver-investigate-pagefault"  :thumbsup:

ci-bot: rerun queued: a100-smoke #4421.1 (driver=525.105.17) — queued on node-selector:a100-canary — link: https://ci.internal/reports/4421/1

liam: if the pinned run passes, that points at a recent runtime/driver rollout. if it still flakes, we should bisect the PRs that touched batching and also try a local repro with the same runtime on a spare rig. I can spare time later today to help reproduce.

priya: noted. I'll kick the non-batched run now and also schedule a repro on our dev-a100 rig overnight. posting the command I'm running in case others want to reuse:
```
python tools/run_smoke.py --model v1.8.2 --batching off --device cuda:0 --repeat 50
```

priya: quick check result: non-batched rerun started. will report outcome ~in 30m.

sasha: if it reproduces locally, capture: nvidia-smi -q, dmesg, /proc/interrupts, and the exact container runtime output (LD_PRELOAD, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, etc). also run with CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 to get deterministic stack traces.

priya: ack — will collect those.

ryan: one more ask: if pinned rerun passes, can we hold canary rollout of the cuda12-rolling tag until we confirm stable? switching the canary policy to "hold" avoids more flakes spamming CI.

priya: agreed. I'll set canary rollout to hold for gpu-runtime:cuda12-rolling now.

priya: update: pinned rerun passed (all checks green). non-batched run also passed. looks like runtime/driver mismatch is likely.

liam: good find. let's open a followup to pin runtime in the infra images and add a smoke that exercises the batching hotpath under both old/new drivers. i'll make the infra issue and tag infra-eng.

priya: filing infra ticket: INFRA-1283 — pin gpu-runtime drivers for canary and add batching smoke matrix. tagging @infra-eng. link: https://issues.internal/INFRA-1283

ryan: thanks — can we also add a short healthcheck that runs a single step of our batching path at node boot so driver/runtime skew gets caught earlier?

priya: adding note to INFRA-1283. I'll follow up tomorrow with repro artifacts from the dev rig (dmesg, nvidia-smi, profile). thanks everyone for the quick help! :pray:

sasha: nice triage. if it recurs after the infra change we'll do a bisect across recent runtime builds. :eyes:

ci-bot: a100-smoke #4421.1 finished: PASS (driver=525.105.17)

priya: closing for now — will reopen if repro yields more.
